He's given me an ultimatum: either I prove the missed dinner was an involuntary physiological failure, or I quit the overnight role. My question is straightforward: does acute sleep deprivation cause involuntary failures of prospective memory?

I’ll look up the sleep-science literature on prospective memory so the answer is grounded in actual studies, not just a hunch. I’ll also check whether anything in your prior context changes how this should be framed.
